it('routes the quick links through the hash router', async () => {
    renderPage()

    fireEvent.click(await screen.findByRole('button', { name: 'Navigation route' }))
    expect(window.location.hash).toBe('#/maps/navigation-route')

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Geofences' }))
    expect(window.location.hash).toBe('#/maps/geofences')

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Locations' }))
    expect(window.location.hash).toBe('#/maps/locations')
  })

confirmed_findings.mechanism: Each action changes only window.location.hash, leaving /live as the pathname. The mounted router is BrowserRouter, not HashRouter. App routes are /navigation, /geofences and /locations, not /maps/*; the source search found no routing hash bridge. The test asserts fragment strings in MemoryRouter rather than destination routing.

reproduction.mode: synthetic source walkthrough only; no application, tests, locations or requests used
steps: Start on the source-defined /live route with synthetic cached page data.
Trace each click handler: pathname remains /live while its fragment becomes the hardcoded #/maps/... value.
reproduction.expected: Each action navigates to its registered destination while preserving intended selected-vehicle scope and navigation guards.
reproduction.observed_source_path: Each action changes only window.location.hash, leaving /live as the pathname. The mounted router is BrowserRouter, not HashRouter. confirmed_findings.fix: Use the existing guarded/link/router navigation contract and registered paths; replace the hash-only assertion with real destination routing coverage in the authorized page test.
